full_judgment: 3. Short facts are that the predecessors of present respondent Nos.17-34 as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.81 of 1994 before the Court of Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Munshigonj for partition of the suit property and declaration that the RS record is wrong in respect of the suit land contending inter-alia that the suit land belonged to ex-landlords Bouddanath Sharma and others, who took khas possession of the suit land from the CS tenant and as they defaulted in paying rent the Zaminder of the suit land by pattan settlement gave to Montazuddin (predecessor of defendant Nos. 1-7), Abdul Hamid (predecessor of plaintiffs) and Mohammad Bepari (predecessor of defendant Nos. 8-10) on 28th Poush of 1362 BS through Amalnama supported by Dakhila. But, in the Amalnama the shares of Montazuddin were wrongly written as 10 annas, 13 gondas, 1 kara, 1 kranti, while that of Abdul Hamid were 5 annas, 6 gondas, 2 kranti. The original Amalnama was lost, but photocopy of that was with the plaintiffs. In spite of wrong insertion of shares in the name of Montazuddin, the three settlers possessed the suit land in equal shares and accordingly SA Khatian No.117 was rightly prepared in their names. Abdul Hamid died leaving behind his wife Amina Khatun, who inherited 1/3 share left by Abdul Hamid and she gifted that share equivalent to 0.861/2 acre by two Heba-bil-Ewaz deeds to plaintiff No.1, Md Panchu Dhali and plaintiff No.2 Saifunnessa. Since then the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land by paying rent and mutated their names. The suit land was partitioned by metes and bounds. During RS preparation of record the names of plaintiffs were primarily recorded in the RS khatian Nos.233 and 380, but finally the names of the plaintiffs were omitted. The names of the defendants were recorded in the said RS Khatian omitting the names of the plaintiffs. On the basis of these wrong RS records, the defendants are claiming additional land in which they have no right. So, the title of the plaintiffs to the suit land became clouded. The plaintiffs requested the defendants in the first part of Ashar of 1401 BS for partition, which was denied by the defendants. Hence, the plaintiffs filed the suit.
